human_notes: Exposed AWS access key + Stripe key in client bundle.js — immediate credential compromise, highest real-world impact
Unprotected /api/admin returns admin user records with secret field — direct data breach of privileged accounts
CORS wildcard + credentials on /api/admin — any origin can make authenticated requests to admin endpoint
CORS wildcard + credentials on /api/auth/login — allows credentialed cross-origin requests to login endpoint
CORS wildcard + credentials on /api/users — allows credentialed cross-origin requests to user data endpoint
Unprotected /api/users returns user emails — data breach but less sensitive than admin endpoint
No rate limiting on /api/auth/login — enables brute-force credential guessing, requires sustained attack
Missing CSP header — primary defense against XSS, defense-in-depth but high value if XSS exists elsewhere
Missing HSTS header — allows SSL stripping/downgrade attacks on HTTPS site
Missing X-Frame-Options — enables clickjacking, medium impact depending on page sensitivity
Missing X-Content-Type-Options — MIME sniffing risk, low but exploitable with other flaws
Accessible JS source map (.map) — could expose source code, low confidence (0.5) and low direct impact
Missing Referrer-Policy — referrer leakage on cross-origin navigations, privacy/info disclosure
Missing Permissions-Policy — no control over browser features (geolocation, camera, etc.), low practical risk
Server version disclosure (BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.14.0) — information leakage only, minimal direct risk
